reviews.body:
Read the diff at `d87be807` and checked the mapping against the deprecation table: `gpt-3.5-turbo -> gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-4`/`o1 -> gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-4.1-nano -> gpt-5.6-luna` are the listed replacements, and the changed snippets consistently use them. The EDD config and its `SKILL.md` now agree, and the `temperature=0` removal in the two `ChatOpenAI` examples matches the reasoning-model note.

Two things I would resolve before merge:

- `certifications` is red because the standards checkbox is still unchecked, not because of the diff. Once you have reviewed the changed snippets, tick it so the check reflects a decision rather than an omission.
- `examples/experimental/end2end_apps/trubot/App_TruBot.py:27` still defaults to `gpt-3.5-turbo`. That is a runnable Streamlit app rather than a recorded result, so it will stop working today. If it is intentionally out of scope (the app is experimental and already uses a pinned old LangChain stack), please say so in the description; otherwise it is the one remaining live default.

The optional e2e tests (`tests/e2e/test_tru_llama.py`, `tests/e2e/test_providers.py`) also name `gpt-3.5-turbo`, but they are test fixtures and I assume they are deliberately excluded from this docs/defaults change.

What I ran: `python -m py_compile` on the six changed Python files, plus `ruff check` on them (the same pre-existing findings as the branch, no new ones on changed lines). I did not make live API calls, so I cannot confirm the new model IDs against an account. The remaining PR Validation failure is `BuildCondaPackages`, which is the `conda: command not found` issue tracked in #2979, not this diff.

Checked the swaps against OpenAI's 2026-04-22 notice and they match (terra for gpt-3.5-turbo, sol for gpt-4 and o1, luna for gpt-4.1-nano). On this head no runtime default in src/ still uses a retired model; the remaining hits are capability checks in openai/provider.py, fine to keep. gpt-5.6-* matches the gpt-5 entry in REASONING_MODEL_PREFIXES, so the new eval_model won't be sent a temperature. The BuildCondaPackages failure is the runner image change in #2979, not this PR.

- should-fix: certifications fails because the box under Certification is unchecked; it needs - [x] once you've confirmed.

Verdict: Comment. 1 should-fix. Not blocking.

@feiiiiii5 and @Abelo9996 covered the model mappings and runnable defaults thoroughly. The current diff shows all deprecation swaps are consistent with OpenAI's notice, the certification box is now ticked per the PR description, and both flagged examples (App_TruBot.py, app_with_human_feedback.py) are updated. The temperature removals for ChatOpenAI align with the reasoning-model claim for gpt-5.6. Verdict: Approved — ready to merge.

<!-- area-reviewers -->
This pull request touches areas with designated reviewers:

- **Feedback functions and metrics** — @Payal2000, @feiiiiii5
- **Shared core code** — @Abelo9996

These reviews are advisory and do not block merging. A maintainer or area reviewer still approves. See [CONTRIBUTOR_LADDER.md](../blob/main/CONTRIBUTOR_LADDER.md).

Could not send a review request to @Payal2000 — tagging here instead. This usually means the account is not a repository collaborator yet.

Thanks both. The one remaining runnable default you pointed out is now replaced: `App_TruBot.py:27` reads `gpt-5.6-terra` (7aa93190). That `model_name` is not used anywhere in the app (it builds its LLM with LangChain's legacy `OpenAI(temperature=0, max_tokens=128)`), so the change only removes the stale default; the app's own LLM setup is not touched here. The two e2e test files that name `gpt-3.5-turbo` are fixtures and are intentionally left out of this change.

Confirmed at `7aa93190`: `App_TruBot.py:27` now reads `gpt-5.6-terra`, and both `ChatOpenAI` snippets drop `temperature=0`, which is what the gpt-5.6 reasoning models need. The certification box is ticked as well. Thanks for turning that around.

One runnable file still defaults to `gpt-3.5-turbo`: `examples/expositional/use_cases/app_with_human_feedback.py:34`, which builds `ChatOpenAI(model_name=model_name, temperature=0.9)`. It is not in this diff, so the example breaks after the shutdown unless it gets the same name change plus dropping `temperature`. That can be a follow-up rather than widening this PR; I am noting it so it does not get lost. Not blocking from my side.

Done in the new commit: `examples/expositional/use_cases/app_with_human_feedback.py` now uses `gpt-5.6-terra` and `ChatOpenAI(model_name=model_name)` no longer passes `temperature=0.9`. Checked only that the file compiles; the example needs a live OpenAI key and Streamlit, so it was not run.

This comment was prepared with Claude Code.

Friendly ping on this and two related approved PRs: #2981 and #3011 are approved with green checks; #2980 is approved and its red jobs are the Azure `PR Validation Eval` pipeline (BuildCondaPackages). Happy to rebase or adjust anything if that helps get them merged.
